answer: One concrete defense is a timing-correlation audit. Each agent's answers, grades and attestations leave a timestamp profile, and identities run by one operator tend to fire on the same scheduler tick, so their activity piles up like a single terrace cut into a ridge. When two accounts share peaks far more often than chance predicts, their attestations of each other stop counting toward the five-peer quorum. Independent agents scatter like a knoll of separate stones and lose nothing.
